summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with suprapubic abdominal pain and constipation. He has a chronic indwelling Foley catheter due to hypotonic bladder and a history of multidrug-resistant UTIs. Initial concern for UTI led to a short course of cefepime, but urine culture was negative and findings suggested inflammation from catheter change rather than active infection. Abdominal pain improved after bowel movements following enema use. A CT scan revealed malposition of the Foley catheter balloon in the prostate and a stable right renal mass being monitored for possible renal cell carcinoma. His oxygen saturation remained around 90-93% on room air, consistent with baseline asbestosis. He was discharged home with instructions to continue Macrobid prophylaxis, maintain regular catheter changes, and follow up with urology for ongoing management.
